title: Ivo and the Promise
premise: Edmund Joubert, a ghostwriter who faked her death twelve years ago to escape a scandal that destroyed her family, has survived by writing other people's truths while burying her own—most faithfully in ten years of anonymous letters to a dying stranger she never expected to meet. When the letters' recipient, Ivo Marchetti, moves in next door and begins searching for his mysterious correspondent, Edmund must decide whether the woman who hid to survive can risk being seen. As Ivo's illness advances and her ghostwriting assignment forces her to betray him professionally, their intimacy deepens into something neither planned. In the end, Edmund publishes her own memoir under her real name, choosing visibility over safety, and stays beside Ivo through his final year—learning that love's promise isn't permanence but presence.
about_author: V. M. Fairweather is the pen name of a former obituary writer who spent a decade composing other people's endings before attempting her own beginnings. She lives quietly on the coast of Maine, where she still answers every letter by hand.

chapters.title: The Ghostwriter's Hand
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She finishes ghosting a celebrity chef's memoir, erasing herself so thoroughly even her editor doesn't know her face. Establishes her ritualized invisibility: no photos, no surname, rent paid in cash. Emotional beat: competent loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: Letters to a Stranger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, with flashbacks. We learn of the decade of letters she wrote to a hospital patient named only 'I.M.,' begun as a charity assignment and continued because he wrote back. The correspondence ended eight months ago when replies stopped. Beat: tenderness she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The New Neighbor
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A moving van arrives next door; she watches from behind curtains as a thin man with a cane directs boxes. When he introduces himself as Ivo Marchetti, she nearly drops her mail. Beat: terror disguised as coincidence.

chapters.title: Twelve Years Ago
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Recovering from surgery, Ivo recalls how his nurse read him the first letter aloud and how writing back became his reason to endure treatment. He came to this town because the postmark was here. Beat: hope as a discipline.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She rehearses excuses while Ivo knocks with borrowed sugar, probing gently about whether she knows anything about letters. She lies fluently and hates herself for it. Beat: the cost of the mask, paid daily.

chapters.title: The Rival's Memoir
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Her new contract: ghostwrite the memoir of Julian Ashe—a bestselling author whose rise twelve years ago was built on plagiarizing Edmund's dead brother's manuscript. Writing it means excavating everything she buried. Beat: old grief reopened.

chapters.title: Garden Conversations
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Over a shared fence, Edmund and Ivo trade stories that are true but not complete—he omits the letters, she omits her past. Their ease frightens her more than suspicion would. Beat: intimacy without identity.

chapters.title: What the Letters Said
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. He rereads the letters seeking clues to her location and realizes the writer knew his hometown, his sister's name, his fear of water. He begins testing Edmund with details. Beat: the net tightening, tenderly.

chapters.title: Julian's Version
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Interviewing Julian, she hears him claim her brother's story as inspiration and realizes the memoir could either expose or sanctify the theft. Her editor wants warmth, not truth. Beat: rage channeled into craft.

chapters.title: The Diagnosis
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A scan shows the cancer has returned aggressively; months, perhaps less. He decides finding his letter-writer matters more than treatment schedules. He asks Edmund to drive him to appointments. Beat: urgency sharpening every moment.

chapters.title: Almost Told
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the hospital, a nurse recognizes Ivo and mentions 'the letter lady.' Edmund nearly confesses; instead she deflects, and the lie lands between them like glass. Beat: self-betrayal at the worst hour.

chapters.title: First Kiss, Second Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. After a storm knocks out power, they kiss by candlelight—and Ivo says he wishes the letter-writer could see him now. Edmund says nothing. Beat: joy contaminated by concealment.

chapters.title: The Manuscript Trap
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. To finish Julian's book she must quote the stolen manuscript, which means signing an affidavit denying its true origin—the same affidavit used against her brother. Signing would make her complicit again. Beat: history demanding a second payment.

chapters.title: Ivo Investigates
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Using a librarian friend, he traces the letters' handwriting style to a ghostwriting credit buried in Julian Ashe's acknowledgments. The name listed is Edmund Joubert. Beat: revelation arriving like sunrise.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Fence
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Ivo asks why she let him fall in love with a stranger while standing right there. Edmund finally tells him everything: the scandal, her brother's suicide, the death of her old name. Beat: raw exposure, anger braided with relief.

chapters.title: Silence Between Houses
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Days of silence. Ivo wrestles with feeling chosen second—to the letters, to the past; Edmund drafts a confession letter she cannot send. Beat: grief doing the work honesty postponed.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Too weak to visit, Ivo writes Edmund a final letter in the style of their old correspondence, forgiving her and asking one thing: write your own story before mine ends. Beat: forgiveness as invitation.

chapters.title: Refusing the Affidavit
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She tears up the affidavit, quits Julian's project publicly, and sends the exposé—including her brother's original pages—to a journalist, attaching her real name. Beat: burning the mask for fuel.

chapters.title: Under Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She begins her memoir, 'Ivo and the Promise,' in his hospice room, reading each page aloud as he edits. The scandal breaks; her old life resurfaces; she lets it look. Beat: authorship reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Promise Kept
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Ivo's decline accelerates; they marry quietly in the garden between their houses, witnesses two neighbors and a notary. He asks her to keep writing after. Beat: love as covenant, not cure.

chapters.title: After
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Ivo dies on a morning in October holding the finished manuscript. She reads his marginalia—one word per chapter, all variations of 'yes.' Beat: sorrow fully inhabited, not escaped.

chapters.title: Published
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, epilogue. At her first public reading, she signs books with her real name and finds a letter in the audience—from Ivo, arranged before his death, to be delivered today. It says: you kept it. Beat: survival transformed into testimony.
